notes:
The launcher had every part working and still looked like something side-loaded. This rebuild is the visual layer only - no change to the overlay window manager, the CAN service or the updater.

The single biggest cause was invisible: the interface scale defaulted to 0.8, so the display density was multiplied down and every size in the app arrived twenty percent smaller than it was written. A body size set at 20 reached the eye at 16. Four earlier releases were spent making text bigger inside a system that was quietly shrinking all of it. The default is now 1.0 and the panel is finally the 1600x1000 canvas it actually is.

No third-party app icon is shown anywhere any more. A photorealistic RCA cable for AUX, a glossy blue squircle for Bluetooth and an orange gradient badge for TPMS were three unrelated visual languages sitting side by side, none of them this app's. There are now twenty-five icons drawn to one specification - one stroke weight, one corner treatment, one colour - and where no icon exists yet a tile shows the app's initials in the display face rather than borrowing someone else's artwork.

Tile backgrounds were the average colour of the app's icon, which is why they were brown and tan: averaging the red, green, yellow and blue of an RCA plug lands in mud every time. That code is deleted, and the fields it wrote to are gone too, so it cannot come back.

Surfaces are properly near-black now with real separation between layers, and hairlines are pushed harder than looks right on a monitor because this screen is read through a windscreen in daylight. Every colour is checked against every surface it can land on by a test that runs on each build; it moved four values that looked fine by eye, including the warning red, which passed on the background and failed on the raised panels where a warning actually appears.

The music widget was one of the largest things on screen while saying "Nothing playing". It is now a strip of fixed height that never resizes - artwork, title and controls all fit inside the same box, so nothing on the screen moves when music starts.

The eight small icons along the bottom are gone. In their place is a nav rail on the right edge - right, because the truck is right-hand drive and that is the near edge for the driver - with five large icons and a single accent bar that slides to show where you are. That bar is the only accent-coloured thing on the screen. Green, amber and red now belong to the vehicle and nothing else.

There is still no CAN data on this van, so every reading is designed for that. A missing value is an em dash set in the numeric face at full size, not an orange NO SENSOR DATA label and never a zero pretending to be a reading. Because the placeholder takes a real digit's width, nothing will shift by a pixel when the bus finally starts talking.

Two typefaces are bundled - Space Grotesk for words, JetBrains Mono for every number - subset down to 152 KB in total, which is why the app grew by only 0.11 MB.

Six screen states are rendered to PNG at the true panel resolution and committed, and any future change that disturbs them fails the build. Every fix above came from looking at those renders.

Settings still works but has not been rebuilt yet; the theme control there is now Auto, Day or Night, with Auto following the headlights.
